original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a single aperture Ka or Q/V band gateway multibeam antenna, capable to serve multiple satellites located in a large field of view.Targeted Improvements: Replacing multiple (up to 12) gateway antennas based on reflectors with a single aperture multi-beam gateway antenna ; Reducing by a factor 10 the complexity ofa conventional active array antenna.Description: With the proliferation of satellite constellations, there is a strong interest, need, and market opportunities for innovative multibeam antennas for Gateway stations. These antennas should be able to generate multiple simultaneous beams in order to guarantee the link with different satellites. Existing gateway antennas are mainly based on reflectors dishes repointable mechanically, and able to track a single satellite instantaneously. Multibeam gateway antennas based onactive phased arrays are also under development. They can generate multiple simultaneous beams, but they are not competitive yet interms of complexity, power dissipation, thermal issues, cost. For these reasons, in this activity innovative multibeam antennas with a reduced complexity should be developed. The beamforming could be analogue, digital or hybrid. A significant simplification can be obtained by limitingthe multiple beams directions in a limited portion of the field of view where the majority of the satellitesareexpected to be visible. In facts, the number of active controls in the antenna is proportional to the extension of the angular field of view. Another simplification can be obtained by assuming a minimum angular separation between two contiguous beams corresponding to two different satellites. The design must be customisable based on the longitude and latitude of the gateway station considering also the orbital position and orientation of the constellations to be served. By applying these simplifications and customisations, significant simplifications in the gateway antennas should be obtained.The activity will design, manufacture and test a singleaperture Ka or Q/V band gateway multibeam antenna, capable to serve multiple satellites located in a large field of view. At least twopromising technical solutions will be identified and studied. Trade-offs will be carried out and the most promising concept willbe selected and implemented in a reduced scale prototype. The developed multibeam gateway antenna will be tested in a relevant environment establishing a link with a real satellite and scanning two independent andsimultaneous beams.

original.description: This activity investigates concepts for providing on-demand PNT services during crises by leveraging satellite communication systems. It aims to support continuity of positioning, navigation, and timing when terrestrial infrastructures fail due to natural disasters or humanitarian emergencies. The study will identify relevant use cases, define system concepts and requirements, and assess feasibility through preliminary designs. It will also demonstrate key components and functions via small-scale laboratory proof-of-concept setups. The outcome will include a mission study, roadmap, and verification report for future demonstrations. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

original.description: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
